description: A four-bit decoder with a latch: the four inputs are read as a number from 0 to 15 on a strobe, and the one output matching that number is driven low while the other fifteen are high.

inputs.text: The least significant bit of the number being decoded, worth one.
The second bit of the number being decoded, worth two. The maker's tooltip calls this the most significant bit, which it is not.
The third bit of the number being decoded, worth four.
The most significant bit of the number being decoded, worth eight. The maker's tooltip names this jack B, though the panel prints IN D.
A rising edge reads the four input bits and latches the number; between strobes the outputs hold what that number selected.
While this is high every output is driven high and the latched number is ignored.

outputs.text: 0V while the latched number matches this output's own number and the inhibit input is low; 10V the rest of the time.

notes: A logic input counts as high once it rises above 2V and does not count as low again until it falls below 0.1V; a logic output is 10V for high and 0V for low.
Nothing reaches the outputs until a rising edge arrives at the strobe input; with nothing patched there the latched number stays at 0 and output S0 is the selected one.
